title: Slot-escrow reservation advisor and deferred zipper compaction for spatial KV reuse
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: high-percentile prefill + decode latency spikes on multi-tenant hosts caused by frequent small evictions and scattershot rehydration of KV fragments. Existing LRU-like eviction mixes hot small fragments with adjacent free holes which increases fragmentation and decoding work when requests rehydrate across many micro-slices. This ticket introduces two coordinated runtime features: 1) a lightweight 'slot-escrow' reservation layer that temporarily reserves neighboring slots for the same tenant/segment to reduce immediate reallocation churn during transient load, and 2) a deferred 'zipper compaction' advisor that performs low-priority, spatial packing of nearby fragments during low-load windows to reduce fragmentation and improve future decode throughput. The goal is to reduce 99th prefill latency and end-to-end decode work without increasing steady-state memory overhead or harming fairness across tenants.
rationale: Empirical traces from internal staging (dashboard 'kv/hotset-frag-2026-02') show that 60% of tail prefill cost comes from requests that miss on 4+ fragments for the same token span. Microbenchmarks indicate that co-locating those fragments into contiguous slots reduces kernel warmup and scatter IO by ~28% on average. A hard eviction-only policy optimizes for immediate occupancy but increases long-term decode cost; slot-escrow reduces churn by providing a short reservation grace-period while zipper compaction recovers fragmentation opportunistically when the cluster is quiet.
design_decisions: Slot-escrow is bounded (max 200ms reservation per logical allocation) and charged against a per-tenant escrow budget to avoid long-lived soft-reservations
Escrow reservations can be preempted if host memory pressure crosses critical watermark (failsafe to preserve global SLOs)
Zipper compaction runs as a background job with configurable throttles and an adaptive scoring function that prefers compaction ranges with high touch-density and high decode-cost savings
Compaction advisor exposes a signal to the kernel selector so it can co-schedule contiguous kernel runs (microfusion) when fragments are compacted
No changes to on-disk state are required; this is an in-memory reindexing/slot migration scheme with idempotent recovery semantics
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Instrumentation - add escrow reservation counters and touch-density heatmap (ENG-315999-1)
Phase 2: Escrow module - implement reservation lifecycle, budget enforcement, preemption hooks (ENG-315999-2)
Phase 3: Zipper advisor - compute compaction candidates, scoring, and safe-move plan (ENG-315999-3)
Phase 4: Move executor - implement slot-copy/atomic-swap primitive + kernel hinting for microfusion (ENG-315999-4)
Phase 5: End-to-end testing, perf benchmarks, and gradual rollout (canary then host-tier rollout)
test_plan: Unit tests: escrow lifecycle, budget accounting, preemption behavior
Integration: synthetic replay with trace 'kv/hotset-frag-2026-02' verifying 99p prefill reduction >= 15%
Chaos: preemption under host pressure and crash-recovery exercises to validate idempotent slot moves
Benchmark: compare decode kernel invocation counts and end-to-end token cost under medium and burst load profiles
Safety: ensure tenant fairness by measuring cross-tenant hit-rate regressions (target: no regression > 1%)
rollout_plan: Toggle-gated feature controlled by runtime flag (default=off in prod)
Canary: enable on 5% of hosts in staging-equivalent region for 48h
Measure: collect escrow occupancy, compaction throughput, 95/99 prefill latency, and kernel warmstart counts
Gradual: 5% -> 25% -> 75% -> 100% with 24-72h observation windows and abort-on-regression policy
Fallback: immediate disable path; move executor operations are idempotent and can be rolled back by pausing compaction and letting churn naturally reclaim
metrics: 99th prefill latency (target improvement >= 15% in affected hosts)
Average decode kernel invocations per request (target -20%)
Compaction bytes moved per hour (to monitor background overhead)
Escrow reservation hit-rate and average reservation duration
Cross-tenant fairness delta on hit-rate (target < 1% regression)
